alert_news.title: India's First Geothermal Power Project in an Island Region
bullets: India's first geothermal power project in an island region to be developed in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Ltd inviting Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from agencies to undertake geothermal resource assessment, exploration, and potential power plant development.
The project aims to reduce the islands' dependence on diesel imports and provide indigenous, weather-independent baseload renewable power, improving long-term energy security for the islands.

The proposed programme will begin with geological, geophysical, and geochemical investigations, followed by exploratory drilling, resource validation, and subject to successful resource confirmation, the development of a geothermal power plant.

alert_news.title: Uttar Pradesh: Parichha Weir Gets ICID Heritage Recognition
bullets: Parichha Weir in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, becomes India's first World Heritage Irrigation Structure (WHIS) designated by the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage (ICID).
The 140-year-old Parichha Weir is a rubble-stone masonry structure stretching 1,174 metres and standing 16.8 metres above the riverbed, with a reservoir capacity of 2,400 million cubic feet.
The Betwa Canal system associated with the weir extends about 2,654 km and irrigates 4,28,360 hectares across five districts in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

alert_news.title: Kerala Police launches 'My Police Station' initiative with dedicated help desks
bullets: Kerala Police launches 'My Police Station' initiative with dedicated complaint, women's, children's, senior citizens', transgender, persons with disabilities, cybercrime, and legal-aid help desks.
Police stations will have assistance for applications, online services, RTI-related information, and obtaining FIR copies.
Appointment of young Sub-Inspectors as Station House Officers, with 63 women Sub-Inspectors taking charge as SHOs, is a major change.

alert_news.title: India's First University-led National Space Technology Conclave
bullets: India's first university-led National Space Technology Conclave (NSTC) 2026 is being organized by Chandigarh University's Kalpana Chawla Centre for Research in Space Science and Technology (KCC) in collaboration with ISRO and IIST.

The conclave will focus on the theme 'Emerging Space Technologies for India's Future Space Missions' and will feature 30 distinguished scientists, mission leaders, and technologists from ISRO, IIST, IN-SPACe, NSIL, and URSC, along with 10 CEOs and senior leaders from leading Indian space industries and start-ups.

The conclave will provide a platform for students to engage with space experts and will feature five roundtables and space technology demonstrations, facilitating discussions on the technologies shaping India's next phase of space exploration and human spaceflight.

alert_news.title: Punjab Police's Sadak Surakhya Force to become India's first 3D policing model
bullets: Punjab Police's Sadak Surakhya Force (SSF) will become India's first 3D policing model by integrating drones, satellite imagery, and artificial intelligence (AI) powered predictive systems.
The 3D policing model will create real-time situational awareness, anticipate risks, and support faster police response, making overall traffic and road safety policing more versatile.

The SSF will extend its coverage from 5,500 km to 6,000 km of state roads and aims to build an integrated road safety ecosystem combining satellite data, AI, drones, and geospatial technologies by 2047.

alert_news.title: Prakriti Gyan Dham: India's First Eco-Educational Hub
bullets: Prakriti Gyan Dham is India's first-of-its-kind eco-educational hub, an interactive, open-air facility located at Maharishi Parashar Bioresource Centre (MPBC) in Banthra, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

Developed by CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), it aims to extend scientific research beyond institutional laboratory walls into society, fostering experiential environmental education and preserving botanical-cultural heritage.

Key features include the PAaVan Path (Heritage Trail), Indian Heritage Garden with Interactive QR Systems, The Bamboosteum, Conservation Enclaves (Vibhav & Bhairav), and Lab-to-Society Technology Transfer.

alert_news.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Developed by Skyroot Aerospace
bullets: India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, was developed by Skyroot Aerospace, a Hyderabad-based company.

The rocket was designed and developed by a team of 14 Keralite engineers, including Nirmal Nelson, Ajith Kumar S, Dr Binet Monachan, Ajin Ghosh K, Ranjith Ravi, Lint C Thomas, Anjali Ashokan, Vaisakh V, Ramshij M, Anantha Krishnan, Vishnu M K, Sreenath S, Rahul Ramesh, and Alexis J Neerakkal.

alert_news.title: India's First Generative-AI Powered Government e-Marketplace (GeMAI)
bullets: India's first generative-AI powered government e-marketplace (GeMAI) launched by GeM in May 2025.
GeMAI aims to enable intelligent procurement through AI technology, building on GeM's existing tech infrastructure.
GeM is a government e-marketplace that facilitates procurement of goods and services for the Indian government.

alert_news.title: V.O.C. Port Becomes India's First Scope-2 Emission-Free Major Port
bullets: V.O.C. Port in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, became India's first major port to achieve Scope-2 Emission-Free status on 10 August 2026.
The port secured ISO 50001:2018 certification for its Energy Management System, with renewable energy meeting 93.89% of its total electricity consumption in the 2025-26 financial year.
V.O.C. Port has active green infrastructure including 7.04 MW of solar capacity and 2 MW of wind capacity, with plans for additional renewable energy projects.

alert_news.title: India's First AI Generation: Gen Z
bullets: India's first generation to step into higher education and the workplace in the age of AI is Gen Z.
Gen Z is growing up in an era where AI is evolving at a remarkable speed, and they are the first to begin their professional journey alongside AI.
India's demographic dividend will remain a statistic unless it is transformed into an economic and an AI dividend, which will depend on whether its Gen Z are equipped to thrive in an AI-driven world.

alert_news.title: India's First Experimental Remote Sensing Satellites: Bhaskara-I and Bhaskara-II
bullets: Bhaskara-I and Bhaskara-II (1979-1981) were India's first experimental remote sensing satellites launched by Soviet intercosmos rockets.
These satellites carried TV cameras and Microwave Radiometers (SAMIR) to collect preliminary data on hydrology, forestry, and oceanography.
Bhaskara-I and Bhaskara-II marked the beginning of India's remote sensing capabilities and paved the way for future operational constellations.
